title: Facing the Press — Defeat
notebook: The press room is half full. The correspondents came to watch a victory.
Nadia asks what I say to the forty-six percent who voted yes, and to everyone else.
Explaining sounds like an excuse and context sounds like evasion. That leaves owning it.

narrative.text: The press room is half full. That is the first fact of the morning: the correspondents who came to watch a victory have found something else to watch instead. Nadia Voss is in the front row, second seat from the left. She has a notebook open and a pen in her hand and the expression of someone who has been waiting for exactly this moment.

Chancellor. Forty-six point three percent in favor. Forty-eight point nine against. The Halvek Constitution remains in effect. You staked your government on this document and the country said no. What do you say to the forty-six percent who voted yes — and what do you say to everyone else?

No version of this answer survives contact with the numbers. Forty-six point three. I can explain it, contextualize it, or own it. Explaining sounds like excuse. Context sounds like evasion. That leaves owning it, in front of every camera in the capital.

monologue: No version of this answer survives contact with the numbers. Explaining sounds like excuse. Context sounds like evasion. That leaves owning it, in front of every camera in the capital.

choices.text: "The country said no, and I heard it. Forty-six point three percent believed in this constitution, and I thank them. The rest did not, and I do not dismiss them. A constitution imposed against the will of half the country would not be worth the paper it is written on. We go back to work — with the parliament we have, under the constitution we have, toward the country we still intend to become."

"This vote was forty-six point three percent against a constitution written in the open, and the campaign against it was funded in the dark. I am not conceding the argument. I am conceding the count. There will be another vote — not tomorrow, not imposed, but prepared properly and won honestly. Until then, we govern."

"Ask Kolvar how his forty-eight point nine was assembled — whose money paid for it, and what was promised in return. This referendum was lost in rooms I was not invited into. I will find those rooms."
